title: If You Want to Gather Honey, Don't Kick Over the Beehive
coreMove: Before correcting someone, picture how they already justify their behavior to themselves, and address that picture instead of the behavior.

exampleSpecs.domain: a night-shift charge nurse writing up a younger colleague who missed a medication check
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who supervises people under pressure and is tempted to document their frustration
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the younger nurse shuts down for the rest of the month or actually changes her checklist habit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the charge nurse drafts the write-up, reads it back, and notices she has described the colleague in words the colleague would never use about herself, then rewrites from what the colleague probably told herself at 3am

exampleSpecs.domain: a father at the breakfast table about to confront his sixteen-year-old daughter about a dented car fender
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent who keeps being technically right and losing the kid anyway
exampleSpecs.stakes: the next four years of whether she tells him things or hides them
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the father rehearses the lecture in his head, then remembers the last time his own father said the same sentence to him, and puts the coffee cup down before speaking

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional bakery owner discovering a supplier shorted her flour order by two bags for the third week running
exampleSpecs.audience: a small-business owner who has to keep working with the person she's angry at
exampleSpecs.stakes: the supplier relationship she depends on for Saturday mornings, and her own reputation for being reasonable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner catches herself about to open with an accusation, pauses, and instead asks the delivery driver a question that lets him tell her what went wrong without needing to defend himself

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school band director handing back sheet music to a trumpet player who has been playing the second phrase flat for a month
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher or coach who has corrected the same mistake five times and is losing patience
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the student keeps showing up to rehearsal at all
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director almost says what he has said four times before, sees the student bracing for it, and instead says something that acknowledges how hard the student has been trying before naming the phrase

exampleSpecs.domain: a woman reading a drafted email to her sister about an unpaid loan
exampleSpecs.audience: anyone writing a message while still angry
exampleSpecs.stakes: the family thanksgiving and the loan both
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the first draft lists the sister's failures; the second draft, written after a walk, opens by stating the sister's own stated reason for the delay more generously than the sister herself put it, and only then makes the ask

exampleSpecs.domain: a line cook who just had a tray of prepped onions thrown out by the new sous-chef
exampleSpecs.audience: someone low on the totem pole who has been publicly corrected by a peer
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the cook says something he cannot take back in front of the whole kitchen
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the cook thinks through what the sous-chef must be telling himself about why the onions had to go, and notices that his own urge to fire back is about being seen as competent, not about the onions
